'''James Wilder Orr''' (born [[Huntington, New York|Huntington]], [[New York (state)|New York]], July 19, 1958) is an American fisheries biologist, [[ichthyologist]], [[Systematics|and systematist]] best known for his studies of [[Skate (fish)|skates]], rockfishes, [[snailfish]]es, and [[flatfish]]es. He has described 32 new [[species]] and two new [[genera]] of [[fish]]es, and is the author or co-author of more than 130 scientific and popular articles, including three books. His work has focused primarily on the [[Phylogenetics|phylogenetic]] relationships, [[zoogeography]], [[reproductive biology]], and [[behavior]] of marine [[teleost]]s, particularly deep-water [[Benthic zone|benthic]] taxa. He has spent most of his career at the Alaska Fisheries Science Center, [[National Marine Fisheries Service]] (NMFS), in [[Seattle]], as a Research Fisheries Biologist. At the same time, he has served as an Affiliate Professor at the School of Aquatic and Fishery Sciences, and Affiliate [[Curator]] of Fishes at the [[Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture]], [[University of Washington]], Seattle. For his lifetime of service, Orr was presented with a [[National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration]] (NOAA) Distinguished Career Award in 2022.

== Education ==
Orr graduated from Virgil I. [[Grissom High School (Alabama)|Grissom High School]], [[Huntsville, Alabama|Huntsville]], [[Alabama]] (1976), followed by a B.S. in biology at [[Wheaton College (Illinois)|Wheaton College]], [[Wheaton, Illinois|Wheaton]], [[Illinois]] (1980); a M.S. in [[Fisheries management|Fisheries Management]] at [[Auburn University]], [[Auburn, Alabama|Auburn]], [[Alabama]] (1987); and a Ph.D. in Fisheries at the University of Washington, Seattle (1995).

== Academic contributions ==
Orr's work as a Research Fisheries Biologist for the Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Resource Assessment and Conservation Engineering Division, has focused primarily on the marine [[biodiversity]] of the [[North Pacific Ocean]] especially the [[Bering Sea|Bering]] and [[Chukchi Sea|Chukchi]] seas and waters off southeast [[Alaska]] and the [[Aleutian Islands]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 13, 2019 |title=Feature Story: Meet NOAA Fisheries Biologist Jay Orr. He's made some remarkable discoveries in the deep waters off Alaska |url=https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/feature-story/meet-fisheries-biologist-jay-orr |access-date=July 7, 2023 |website=NOAA Fisheries}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sabri |first=Roya |date=July 13, 2016 |title=Happy accidents: Fisheries researchers net more than they bargain for. Federal biologists meticulously scour the ocean for commercially viable fish. Sometimes, they stumble across truly rare finds |url=https://www.csmonitor.com/Environment/2016/0713/Happy-accidents-Fisheries-researchers-net-more-than-they-bargain-for |access-date=July 7, 2023 |website=The Christian Science Monitor}}</ref> From 1995 to 2013, he participated in NMFS Groundfish surveys, often as Chief Scientist, on the West Coast shelf and slope, [[Gulf of Alaska]] shelf, Aleutian Islands, and Bering and Chukchi seas. New taxa discovered and described by Orr (32 species and two genera) reside mostly in the family [[Liparidae]], but also in the families [[Rajidae]], [[Solenostomidae]], [[Scorpaenidae]], [[Cottidae]], [[Zoarcidae]], [[Ammodytidae]], [[Pleuronectidae]], and [[Oneirodidae]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Joling |first=Dan |date=July 13, 2016 |title=Scientists surveying ocean floor turn up new fish off Alaska: Biologists discover 14 new kinds of snailfish while trawling off the Aleutian Islands |url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/new-fish-alaska-snailfish-aleutians-1.3677184 |access-date=July 7, 2023 |website=Science News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 1, 2019 |title=Feature Story: Rare deep-dwelling skates discovered in Alaska and British Columbia |url=https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/feature-story/rare-deep-dwelling-skates-discovered-alaska-and-british-columbia |access-date=July 7, 2023 |website=NOAA Fisheries}}</ref> He is widely recognized as an expert on the evolutionary history, distribution, [[ecology]], and [[behavior]] of North Pacific fishes in general, but especially the highly species-rich and economically important families [[Rajidae]], Cottidae, Scorpaenidae, and Pleuronectidae.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Orr |first=J.W. |last2=Stevenson |first2=D.E. |last3=with others |date=2011 |editor2-last= |editor2-first= |title=Bathyraja panthera, a new species of skate (Rajidae: Arhynchobatinae) from the western Aleutian Islands, and resurrection of the subgenus Arctoraja Ishiyama |journal=NOAA Professional Papers NMFS |volume=11 |pages=1–50}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Orr |first=J.W. |last2=Kolora |first2=S.R. |last3=with others |date=2021 |title=Origins and evolution of extreme life span in Pacific Ocean rockfishes |journal=Science |volume=374 |pages=842–847}}</ref>

Perhaps his most significant contributions lie in broad-based generic revisions of various taxa, incorporating morphology as well as molecular and early life-history characters;<ref>{{Cite journal Orr has also served as Managing Editor of ''NOAA Technical Reports'' and ''NOAA Professional Papers'', and as Scientific Editor of ''[[Fishery Bulletin]]''. As a Life Member of the [[American Society of Ichthyologists and Herpetologists]], he has served as Index Editor of the Society's journal ''[[Ichthyology & Herpetology]]'' (formerly ''[[Copeia]]'') continuously since 1994. Orr retired at the end of December 2020.

[[Taxa]] named in his honor include a new genus and species, ''Orrichthys longimanus''† Carnevale and Pietsch, 2010 ([[Teleost]]ei: [[Brachionichthyidae]]);<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Carnevale |first=G. |last2=Pietsch |first2=T.W. |date=2010 |title=Eocene Handfishes from Monte Bolca, with description of a new genus and species, and a phylogeny of the family Brachionichthyidae (Teleostei: Lophiiformes) |journal=Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society |volume=160 |issue=4 |pages=621–647}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilkins |first=M. |date=October 11, 2010 |title=Fossil Fish Named After AFSC Scientist Jay Orr |url=https://apps-afsc.fisheries.noaa.gov/Quarterly/ond2010/divrptsRACE3.htm |access-date=July 7, 2023 |website=Resource Assessment & Conservation Engineering (RACE) Division, Groundfish Assessment Program}}</ref> a new species of snailfish, ''Careproctus orri'' Kai and Tashiro, 2021 (Teleostei: Liparidae);<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kai |first=Y. |last2=Endo |first2=H. |last3=Tashiro |first3=F. |last4=Nakayama |first4=N. |date=2021 |title=Two new species of snailfishes of the genus Careproctus (Cottoidei: Liparidae) from the western North Pacific Ocean with a range extension of Careproctus brevipectoralis |journal=Zootaxa |volume=4951 |issue=2 |pages=361–371}}</ref> and a new species of [[sponge]], ''Stelodoryx jamesorri'' Lehnert and Stone, 2020 (Porifera: Poecilosclerida).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lehnert |first=H. |last2=Stone |first2=R.P. |date=2020 |title=Three new species of Poecilosclerida (Porifera, Demospongiae, Heteroscleromorpha) from the Aleutian Islands, Alaska |journal=Zootaxa |volume=4851 |issue=1 |pages=137–150}}</ref>
